Drives the robot with tank controls: left stick runs the left side, right stick the right.

What the library's drive commands (TurnToHeading, DriveToPoint, DriveDistance and the tuning tests) need from your drivetrain.

Timer

Odometry from unpowered tracking wheels (on Rotation Sensors or 3-wire encoders) plus the Inertial Sensor for heading.

Tracking-wheel odometry (TrackingWheelOdometry) corrected by GPS readings.
Trajectory
A time-stamped path for a tank drive: where the robot should be, which way it should face and how fast it should go, every dt seconds.
Trajectory.State
One instant along the trajectory.
Transform2d
A move and turn expressed in a robot's own frame (x forward, y left), like WPILib's Transform2d.
Translation2d
A 2D point / vector in meters.
TrapezoidProfile
A motion profile that accelerates at a constant rate, cruises, then decelerates, like WPILib's TrapezoidProfile.
TrapezoidProfile.Constraints
Speed and acceleration limits, in your units per second and per second squared.
TrapezoidProfile.State
A position and velocity.
Trigger
Binds commands to a condition (usually a button).
TuningCommands
Tests that dial in the drivetrain constants without writing code.
TurnAutoTune
Finds turn PID gains automatically with a relay (bang-bang) test.
TurnToHeading
Turns in place to a FIELD heading (CCW-positive, 0 = +X).
Twist2d
A change in pose along an arc: forward (dx), sideways (dy) and rotation (dtheta, radians).
Units
Unit conversions, same names as WPILib's edu.wpi.first.math.util.Units, plus a few VEX ones (field tiles, GPS millimeters, millivolts, milliamps).
VecBuilder
Same call as WPILib's: VecBuilder.fill(0.1, 0.1, 999) for x, y, heading standard deviations.
Vector3
Three numbers, used for standard deviations (x, y, heading) the way WPILib uses Matrix<N3, N1>.
VexController
Like WPILib's CommandXboxController, for the V5 controller: buttons are Triggers you bind commands to, sticks are -1 to 1, and you can write to the controller's screen and rumble it.
VexController.Axis
The four stick axes.
VexDistanceSensor
V5 Distance Sensor: a laser time-of-flight sensor that reads up to about 2 meters.
VexEncoder
A V5 motor's built-in encoder, like REVLib's RelativeEncoder.
VexGps
V5 GPS Sensor: reads the field-perimeter code strip with a camera and reports where the robot is.
VexInertial
V5 Inertial Sensor, used like a gyro in FRC (Pigeon2, NavX, ADXRS450): VexInertial.getAngle() is clockwise-positive degrees like WPILib's Gyro interface, and VexInertial.getRotation2d() is counter-clockwise-positive for odometry.
VexMotor
A V5 Smart Motor, used like a REV SPARK MAX:
VexMotorConfig
Settings for a VexMotor, built and applied the way REVLib's SparkMaxConfig is:
VexMotorConfig.EncoderConfig
Conversion factors so the encoder reads in your units (meters, degrees...).
VexMotorConfig.IdleMode
What the motor does when stopped.
VexMotorGroup
Several motors that act as one (WPILib's MotorControllerGroup).
VexOpticalSensor
V5 Optical Sensor: color (hue), brightness and proximity at close range (a few cm).
VexRobot
The VEX equivalent of WPILib's TimedRobot.
VexRobot.Mode
 
VexRotationSensor
V5 Rotation Sensor: an absolute encoder, like a REV Through Bore or CANcoder.
Vision
Vision, the way FRC robots do it with PhotonVision: the GPS Sensor is the "camera", a GpsPoseEstimator turns its readings into pose estimates, and each estimate goes to the drive subsystem's pose estimator through the consumer passed in.
WaitCommand
Finishes after a fixed time.
WaitUntilCommand
Finishes when a condition becomes true.
